findings.text: User mode synchronous fault entries share a common surrounding protocol. Each wrapper captures fault related address where shown, marks transition from user context, restores processor interrupt mask to process context value, invokes a dedicated fault routine, then marks return to user context. This shape applies to data aborts, instruction aborts, floating vector accesses, streaming vector accesses, matrix extension accesses, floating exceptions, system register traps, program counter and stack faults, undefined encodings, branch target faults, memory operation faults, guarded control stack faults, invalid vectors and 64 bit breakpoints.

Breakpoint, single step and watchpoint entries from user mode add hardening and debug framing. Breakpoint and single step wrappers apply branch predictor hardening when the trapped program counter indicates kernel range before entering user exit bookkeeping. Breakpoint and watchpoint wrappers bracket their handlers with debug entry and exit, while single step first attempts to complete a suspended breakpoint and only invokes the software step handler when no suspended step completed. Watchpoint is described as the sole debug vector that captures the fault address register.

System call entry from user mode follows a distinct order. It records syscall entry from user state, applies a specific Cortex A76 erratum handler, notifies floating state layer of syscall entry, restores interrupt mask, dispatches to the common SVC routine, then performs syscall exit to user state followed by floating state syscall exit notification.

Common SVC logic preserves the first argument and syscall number, leaves branch type state untouched, and handles tracing and faults in a defined order. A pending asynchronous tag fault indicated by _TIF_MTE_ASYNC_FAULT causes an immediate restartable return without dispatch. When syscall work is pending, a skip number NO_SYSCALL forces a not supported result before entry tracing, and a traced skip jumps directly to exit tracing. After invocation the work flags are rechecked including single step state indicated by _TIF_SINGLESTEP and debug sequence state before deciding whether exit tracing can be skipped.

System call invocation randomizes kernel stack offset, then checks the number against the table size. In range numbers dispatch through the table with an index speculation guard and record the handler result as the return value. Out of range numbers go to an unknown syscall path that first gives compatibility handling a chance and otherwise uses the generic unknown syscall result.

Entry tracing reports to ptrace when emulation or tracing is requested and suppresses dispatch on tracer refusal or emulation, then applies the secure computing gate, then emits a tracepoint when enabled, then records an audit entry with number and first arguments and returns the possibly updated number. Exit tracing records audit exit, emits tracepoint with return value when enabled, reports to ptrace when tracing or single stepping, and processes restartable sequences.

Syscall entry and exit stops distinguish direction by overwriting one general register with a direction marker while saving its prior content for restoration after the stop. The clobbered slot is twelve for compatibility tasks and seven otherwise, with marker PTRACE_SYSCALL_ENTER for entry and marker PTRACE_SYSCALL_EXIT for exit. Consequences documented are that tracer writes to that slot during the stop are discarded, the true value is unavailable during the stop, and syscall stops differ from secure computing and pseudo step traps which preserve registers. Exit handling restores before reporting a pseudo step when single stepping.

Synchronous external abort handling treats non RAS aborts as uncontainable and panics, otherwise consults a severity classifier. Severities ESR_ELx_AET_CE and ESR_ELx_AET_UEO allow progress and return non fatal. Severities ESR_ELx_AET_UEU and ESR_ELx_AET_UER return fatal so the caller panics, with a documented erratum causing certain non virtualized unrecoverable reports to be treated as uncontainable. Severity ESR_ELx_AET_UC and any other value panic directly inside the classifier rather than returning.

The SError panic path is non returning. It marks machine check taint, enables verbose console output, logs the CPU number with syndrome and class string, dumps registers when a register block is present, issues a non maskable panic for asynchronous abort, then parks the CPU in a loop.

Floating point access trap handling checks platform support. When unsupported it injects an illegal instruction fault at the trapped program counter and returns. When supported the fragment treats the trap as impossible and raises a kernel bug.

Streaming vector access handling rejects unsupported platforms and compatibility tasks with an illegal fault, ensures per task vector storage exists and terminates the task when allocation is absent, then takes the per CPU floating context. It atomically claims the vector thread flag TIF_SVE and warns if already claimed. When floating state is live on the CPU it programs the vector length control from the task limit, discards live state and binds the task to the CPU. When state is foreign indicated by TIF_FOREIGN_FPSTATE it converts saved floating registers to vector form, records vector type and flushes task state before releasing context.

Matrix extension access handling rejects unsupported platforms and compatibility tasks with an illegal fault, and rejects traps whose syndrome subfield indicates a mode other than disabled with an illegal fault. It ensures vector and matrix storage exist and terminates the task when either is absent, then takes the per CPU floating context. It atomically claims flag TIF_SME and warns if already claimed. When floating state is live it programs the matrix length control from the task limit and binds the task to the CPU. When state is foreign indicated by TIF_FOREIGN_FPSTATE it flushes task state before releasing context.

Per task vector and matrix storage allocators are idempotent. If storage already exists they optionally clear it to the current size and return. Otherwise they allocate zeroed memory sized for the task. Vector allocation is described as small with an expectation of success, while matrix allocation notes a potentially much larger size.

Conversion from floating to vector form is a no operation unless vector or matrix support exists. Otherwise it derives a length parameter from the task current vector length and copies each floating register into the corresponding vector register slot whose address is base plus per register offset minus base register area offset with endian normalization. Two endian helper variants are present, one transforming by half swaps and one returning input unchanged.

Vector and matrix first access paths hold the per CPU floating context across flag claim and state programming, releasing after handling. Task state flush detaches the task from any CPU, clears its kernel floating pointer, and when floating support exists orders a foreign state flag update with barriers so other CPUs observe detachment before the flag.

Floating exception handling defaults to an unknown floating fault code. When the syndrome indicates valid trap state flagged by ESR_ELx_FP_EXC_TFV it prioritizes invalid operation indicated by FPEXC_IOF, division by zero indicated by FPEXC_DZF, overflow indicated by FPEXC_OFF, underflow indicated by FPEXC_UFF then inexact indicated by FPEXC_IXF into the corresponding floating fault codes, and delivers a floating point fault signal with the chosen code at the user instruction pointer.

System instruction trap handling scans a hook table for the first entry whose masked syndrome equals the expected value and invokes its handler. When no entry matches it falls back to the standard undefined instruction path so newly defined encodings behave consistently.

Undefined instruction handling from user mode first gives AArch32 breakpoint handling a chance, then fetches the trapped encoding, then tries system register emulation and deprecated encoding emulation in order, injecting an illegal fault when fetching fails or no emulation claims the encoding. Instruction fetch distinguishes Thumb mode from 32 bit mode. Thumb fetches a halfword with endian conversion and, when the wide indicator predicate holds, fetches a second halfword and combines them. Otherwise it fetches a word with endian conversion. Fetch failures from user memory report a fault.
The threshold separating narrow and wide 32 bit compatibility encodings is hex value E800, with at or above treated as wide.

Instruction abort, program counter fault, breakpoint and single step entries apply branch predictor hardening before enabling interrupts when the relevant address indicates kernel range. Data abort and most other synchronous wrappers do not perform this check in the shown fragments. Program counter fault checks the instruction pointer while breakpoint and single step check the program counter field and instruction abort checks the fault address.

Several synchronous vectors have fixed fault outcomes. Branch target failure injects illegal instruction fault. Guarded control stack failure injects segmentation fault with protection error code. Invalid synchronous vector records zero fault address with syndrome as fault code then forces illegal fault with a diagnostic. Memory operation handling resets operation registers from syndrome and fast forwards single step state rather than signalling.

Fault to signal mapping observed. Unsupported or mis mode vector, matrix and floating accesses plus undefined, branch target and invalid vectors use SIGILL with ILL_ILLOPC. Floating exceptions use SIGFPE with FPE_FLTINV, FPE_FLTDIV, FPE_FLTOVF, FPE_FLTUND, FPE_FLTRES or FPE_FLTUNK. Guarded stack faults use SIGSEGV with SEGV_CPERR. Missing vector or matrix storage uses SIGKILL. Unknown and skipped traced syscalls use ENOSYS and ERESTARTNOINTR results where shown.

Register and task state touched by the lane includes a register save area carrying general registers, stack pointer, program counter, processor state, original argument and syscall number fields, and per task thread storage carrying fault address and code, floating, vector and matrix state pointers, floating CPU tracking, kernel floating pointer, floating type and saved floating register file. System call dispatch uses slot eight for the number and slot zero for the first argument and return, while trace direction marking uses slot seven natively and slot twelve for compatibility.

Callable interfaces exposed beyond their file in this lane include SError entry and panic helpers, undefined and system trap handlers, vector and matrix and floating access and exception handlers, storage allocators and task flush, invalid vector helper, guarded stack and branch target and memory operation handlers, SVC dispatch, and syscall trace entry and exit helpers.
